name: stri_pad_both
title: Pad a string on both sides

origin.description: Add pad characters on both sides until each string reaches width.
origin.usage: stri_pad_both(str, width = floor(0.9 * getOption("width")), pad = " ", use_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum output widths. The default is 72 under Rscript.

arguments.name: pad
arguments.text: Padding text of display width 1, or one code point when use_length is TRUE.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: TRUE counts code points. FALSE counts display width.

origin.details: Vectorized over str, width, and pad. An odd gap puts the extra pad on the right. Width is display width unless use_length is TRUE. A missing string, width, or pad yields a missing result.
origin.example:
x <- stri_pad_both("ab", 5, pad = "*")
cat(paste0('stri_pad_both("ab", 5, "*") returns ', x, '.\n'))

translation.description: Add pad characters on both sides until each string reaches width.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum output widths. The default is 72 under Rscript.

arguments.name: pad
arguments.text: Padding text of display width 1, or one code point when use_length is TRUE.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: TRUE counts code points. FALSE counts display width.

translation.details: An odd gap puts the extra pad on the right: floor(n/2) copies on the left and the rest on the right. Width is display width from stri_width unless use_length is TRUE. A missing string, width, or pad yields NA. The default width is 72.
translation.value: A string, or NA. A list returns a list. None returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.pad import stri_pad_both
x = stri_pad_both("ab", 5, pad="*")
print(f'stri_pad_both("ab", 5, "*") returns {x}.')
